A ggplot map of three-part compositions, as on CensusMapper

Source: R/cm_tricolore.R
geom_cm_tricolore.Rd

Maps compositions of three parts, e.g. the shares of children, working age population and seniors, in the colours of CensusMapper's ternary ("rgb") maps (see cm_tricolore()), with a triangular colour key: a ggplot2::geom_sf() layer with the colours as fill, and the key as a legend. The key shows the colours of compositions, the first part at the top, the second bottom left and the third bottom right, and the regions as dots.

Usage

geom_cm_tricolore(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  labels = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  center = rep(1/3, 3),
  breaks = 3,
  hue = 60,
  chroma = 200,
  lightness = 80,
  contrast = 0.4,
  spread = 1,
  na.value = "grey60",
  show_data = TRUE,
  key_size = 3,
  show.legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Aesthetics made with ggplot2::aes(): p1, p2 and p3, the three parts, as counts or shares, are required. Others, e.g. colour, are passed on to geom_sf().

data

The data for the layer, sf data; by default the plot's data.

...

Other arguments passed on to ggplot2::geom_sf(), e.g. colour = NA.

labels

Labels for the three parts on the key. By default the expressions for p1, p2 and p3. Long labels are wrapped.

name

The title of the key, by default none.

center

The composition that gets the neutral (grey) colour, e.g. the composition of the whole region. By default the centre of the triangle.

breaks

The number of breaks along each side of the triangle for discrete colours, Inf for continuous colours.

hue

The hue of the first part, in degrees (0 to 360); the other parts are 120 and 240 degrees further.

chroma

The maximum chroma (CIE-LUV, 0 to 200). Above about 75 some colours are outside the sRGB gamut and are clipped.

lightness

The lightness (0 to 100).

contrast

How much less light and chroma compositions near the centre get (0 to 1).

spread

How spread out the colours are around the centre (> 0).

na.value

The colour for regions without a composition.

show_data

Whether to show the regions as dots on the key.

key_size

The width of the key, in cm.

show.legend

Whether to show the key.

Value

An object to add to a ggplot with +.

Details

The fill colours are set directly, not through a fill scale, so the plot can still have a fill scale for other layers. Regions without a composition (missing or negative parts, or a total of zero) are na.value. The compositions are computed from the layer's data, or the plot's data if the layer has none, when the layer is added to the plot.

See also

cm_tricolore() for just the colours.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)
census_data <- get_census("CA21", regions = list(CMA = "59933"),
                          vectors = c(children = "v_CA21_11",
                                      working_age = "v_CA21_68",
                                      seniors = "v_CA21_251"),
                          level = "CT", geo_format = "sf")
ggplot(census_data) +
  geom_cm_tricolore(aes(p1 = children, p2 = working_age, p3 = seniors),
                    labels = c("0 to 14", "15 to 64", "65 and over"),
                    colour = NA) +
  geom_cm_context() +
  coord_sf(datum = NA)
} # }
